info.title: KarryGo Vendor CRM Loyalty API
info.description: Section 8D is a vendor-owned loyalty POINTS ledger. Points are integers. They are not money, not a currency, and not convertible: payment-wallet-service remains the sole monetary authority on the platform and nothing in this API reads, writes, or settles against a wallet. There is deliberately no public earn or redeem endpoint — the earning and redemption engines are service-internal primitives awaiting a trusted producer, and the only vendor-callable movements are a bounded, reason-carrying manual adjustment and a full reversal. No canonical customer PII is stored or returned; a customer is referenced only by their vendor-local CRM profile.

x-authority-boundary: Vendor Service owns the loyalty programme, accounts, points ledger, lots, expiry, reversal, and manual adjustments. payment-wallet-service owns all money. customer-service owns customer identity, canonical PII, privacy decisions, and identity merge. Section 8D emits no payment.*, wallet.*, refund.*, settlement.* or payout.* event and holds no currency, minor-unit amount, or wallet reference.
x-programme-state-contract: DISABLED: configuration and reversal remain available; no earning, redemption, or manual adjustment. PAUSED: configuration, manual adjustment, and reversal remain available; no earning or redemption. ACTIVE: everything is available. Reversal is permitted in every state so a business that switches loyalty off can still correct an entry it posted while it was on.
x-expiry-contract: Expiry is stamped onto a point lot when the credit is issued and is never recomputed. Changing the programme's expiry policy affects future credits only; points a customer already holds keep the window they were issued under, and an identity merge carries each lot's original expiry across unchanged. Points past their expiry are excluded from available_points immediately, whether or not the background sweeper has settled them yet, and every balance-changing command settles due expiry before it acts — a sweeper outage delays bookkeeping without ever letting an expired point be spent.
x-ledger-contract: The ledger is append-only. There is no update or delete operation for a posted entry; corrections are made by posting a compensating REVERSAL entry that references the original. Each entry carries a per-account monotonic sequence and the balance that resulted, so history replays exactly. current_points always equals lifetime_credited_points minus lifetime_debited_points and always equals the sum of remaining points across the account's lots.
x-idempotency-contract: Every command requires an Idempotency-Key header. The same key with the same request replays the stored response; the same key with a different request returns 409. The key is also recorded durably against the posted ledger entry, so exactly-once holds in PostgreSQL and does not depend on a cache surviving. Trusted producer credits are additionally deduplicated by source event reference.
x-privacy-contract: A redacted customer's loyalty account becomes non-actionable and is suppressed from Customer 360 and every ordinary loyalty read. Ledger rows are retained: they contain integer point movements and vendor-local references only, with no personal data to erase, and they are the evidence that a balance was legitimately granted and spent. Marketing suppression and processing restriction never confiscate points — holding a balance is not marketing consent, and withdrawing consent is not forfeiture.
x-scope-contract: A points balance belongs to the business, not to a branch. A branch-scoped actor may read or adjust loyalty only for a customer who has a relationship at one of their branches; a customer outside that reach is reported as not found rather than forbidden, so loyalty lookups cannot be used to discover that another branch's customers exist.
x-out-of-scope: Section 8D implements no loyalty tiers, reward catalogue, voucher or coupon engine, cashback, gift cards, wallet conversion, cash-out, campaign targeting, or automatic order integration. Loyalty is also deliberately absent from the Section 8B segmentation field registry, which remains at 22 fields.

get.description: Returns the programme. A business that has never configured one receives the unwritten defaults at version 0 with configured=false; this read never creates a row.

patch.description: Partial update under optimistic concurrency. expected_version must be 0 for the first write and the current version thereafter; a stale version returns LOYALTY_VERSION_CONFLICT rather than overwriting. Changing the expiry policy never rewrites the expiry of points already issued.

get.description: Returns the balance summary. A customer who has never held points is reported as NOT_ENROLLED rather than as a zero balance, and no account is created by reading. available_points already excludes anything past its expiry.
Paginated ledger, newest first (created_at DESC, sequence DESC). Ordering is fixed and there is no caller-controlled sort. An entry that has since been reversed carries reversed_by_entry_ref.

post.summary: Manually credit or debit a customer's points
post.description: Direction carries the sign; points is always positive. The amount is bounded by the programme's manual_adjustment_limit and a reason is mandatory. The reason is recorded in the audit log only — it never appears in the ledger row, the emitted event, or any log line. A manual credit may enrol a customer who has no account; a manual debit may not, and may not overdraw.

201.description: The posted entry and the resulting balance.

post.description: Posts a compensating REVERSAL entry; the original is never edited or deleted. Exactly one reversal can exist per entry, enforced by a unique index. Only EARN, REDEEM, ADJUSTMENT_CREDIT and ADJUSTMENT_DEBIT are reversible. Reversing a credit requires its lot to be untouched — if the points have been spent or have expired, the reversal is refused with LOYALTY_REVERSAL_POINTS_ALREADY_CONSUMED rather than silently taking points from an unrelated issuance. Reversing a debit restores the exact points to the exact lots that funded it, keeping their original expiry; anything restored past its expiry is expired again in the same transaction rather than becoming freshly spendable.

BearerAuth.description: Vendor staff access token. Business and branch scope are resolved server-side from the session and are never read from the request.

EntryTypeFilter.name: entry_type
EntryTypeFilter.description: Restrict the page to one ledger entry type.

Forbidden.description: The caller does not hold the required permission at a covering scope.

NotFound.description: The customer, account or entry does not exist, or is outside the caller's reach. The two cases are deliberately indistinguishable.

Conflict.description: A version conflict, an idempotency-key conflict, a programme-state refusal, an insufficient balance, or an entry that cannot be reversed.

RateLimited.description: Too many loyalty commands from this business and staff member.

Unavailable.description: Loyalty writes are disabled by feature flag or the commerce kill switch.

LoyaltyEntryType.description: EARN and REDEEM are posted by service-internal primitives for a future trusted producer; EXPIRE by the programme's own expiry rule; MERGE_IN and MERGE_OUT by an authoritative identity merge. Only EARN, REDEEM, ADJUSTMENT_CREDIT and ADJUSTMENT_DEBIT are reversible.

expiry_days.description: Required when expiry_policy is FIXED_DAYS, absent when it is NEVER.

configured.description: False for the unwritten defaults a business has before it first configures loyalty.

clear_expiry_days.description: Send with expiry_policy=NEVER to drop an existing window. NEVER with a window, or FIXED_DAYS without one, is rejected as LOYALTY_INVALID_EXPIRY_POLICY.

expected_version.description: 0 for the first write; the current version thereafter.

available_points.description: The spendable balance. Excludes anything past its expiry whether or not the sweeper has settled it.

pending_expiry_points.description: Already past expiry and unspendable, awaiting settlement. Surfaced so a balance about to drop can be explained rather than appearing to lose points silently.

LoyaltyEntry.description: One immutable ledger row. Command keys and producer source references are deliberately not exposed.

delta_points.description: Signed and never zero. Positive for credits, negative for debits and expiry.

reason_code.description: A coarse machine code such as MANUAL_CREDIT or POINTS_EXPIRED. The operator's free-text reason is never carried here.

points.description: Always positive. Direction carries the sign; a negative value is rejected. Bounded by the programme's manual_adjustment_limit.

reason.description: Mandatory plain-text justification. Recorded in the audit log only.
Mandatory plain-text justification. Recorded in the audit log only. Reversal is always full; partial reversal is not supported.

message.description: Safe for display. Never contains database or internal error text.
